covered_reasons: Serious illness or injury of the traveller, a travelling companion or close family member
Death of traveller, companion or family member
Natural disaster or severe weather making destination uninhabitable
Unexpected job loss (layoff/termination not your fault) or employer-initiated transfer
Transportation strike that cancels your transport
not_covered: Work: employer denies or revokes time off, or work obligations known before purchase (unless the separate 'Cancel for Work Reasons' benefit is held)

layoff_conditions.text: Termination/layoff must not be your fault, employment permanent (not temp/contract), in position at least 1 or 3 years depending on plan; 86% of cancellation policies cover layoff

aca_marketplace_plans.text: Marketplace (ACA) plans are US-only; generally no coverage abroad beyond US territories; some carriers offer limited, non-standard emergency benefits. State Dept recommends separate travel medical insurance.
aca_marketplace_plans.note: No healthcare.gov primary page found stating this; secondary sources only.

medicare.text: Medicare generally does not pay for care outside the US. Exceptions: in the US when an emergency occurs and a foreign hospital is closer; travelling through Canada between Alaska and another state; cruise ship in a US port or within 6 hours of one. Prescription drugs bought abroad not covered.

pricing_model.description: Flat premium per policy: single-trip (priced by age, destination region, duration) or annual multi-trip; not a percentage of trip cost. Excess per claim, optionally waived for extra premium.

sample_premiums.desc: Single trip, no pre-existing conditions, age 25-34, average
sample_premiums.note: Search summary did not tie each figure to a specific URL in the result list; attribution approximate

sample_premiums.desc: Annual multi-trip, no pre-existing conditions, age 25-34, average

UK.cfar_note: CFAR is essentially a US product; no UK CFAR figures found. null.

ghic_ehic.text: Free NHS card. Gives medically necessary state healthcare (cannot reasonably wait until return) on same terms as residents: emergency treatment, chronic/pre-existing condition care, routine maternity care (not travelling to give birth), dialysis and oxygen (pre-arranged). Not covered: repatriation, private care, residents' statutory charges (non-refundable), travel costs. Not a substitute for travel insurance. Valid in EU, plus some other countries (e.g. Switzerland via EHIC, Australia, Montenegro etc.).

pricing_model.description: Flat premium per single trip or annual multi-trip; discounts for holders of Irish private health insurance with medical cover abroad (Blue Insurance).

sample_premiums.desc: Single trip from, 1 day Europe Premier, under 66 with private health insurance
Annual from, Europe Premier, under 66 with private health insurance

ehic.text: Free, from HSE. Public healthcare in EU/EEA (and Switzerland) at free or reduced cost on resident terms; temporary stays; pre-existing conditions; routine maternity care; students for an academic year. Does not cover private healthcare. Digital card in HSE app; physical card within 10 working days.
ehic.validity_note: Not confirmed; Citizens Information page returned 403.

providers: Blue Cross (Ontario Blue Cross / Pacific Blue Cross)

pricing_model.description: Flat premium by age, trip length, destination (US costs more) and medical questionnaire; emergency medical commonly sold standalone or in an all-inclusive package with cancellation.

sample_premiums.note: Age/destination not stated in source summary; low confidence.

Ontario.text: OHIP pays limited emergency amounts for services received outside Canada after 1 Jan 2020: outpatient up to CAD 50/day; inpatient up to CAD 400/day for OR, CCU, ICU, neonatal/paediatric special care, CAD 200/day for lower levels of care. Hemodialysis reimbursement program exists. Page updated 16 Jan 2026.
Ontario.conflict_note: Secondary sources (CBC, CoverMe) say OHIP eliminated out-of-country emergency coverage from 1 Jan 2020 except dialysis (CAD 210/treatment). The official ontario.ca page read on 2026-10-01 still lists the 50/400/200 limits. Unresolved conflict; verify against the live official page before use. Official page preferred.

British_Columbia.text: Emergency hospital care outside Canada: max CAD 75/day. Physician services paid at BC rates. Not covered outside BC: prescriptions, ambulance, non-physician practitioners. Claims within 90 days (physician) / 6 months (hospital). Province advises supplemental travel insurance.

providers: Seguros Monterrey New York Life (international cover via major medical, SGMM)

pricing_model.description: Travel 'asistencia' sold per trip or annual multi-trip, flat price by plan tier/destination; medical limits stated in USD (international) or MXN (domestic).

sample_premiums.note: AXA México site requires quote tool; no published price.

schengen_rule.text: Mexicans needing a Schengen visa must hold travel medical insurance of at least EUR 30,000 covering emergency treatment, hospitalisation and repatriation, valid across Schengen (Reg. (EC) 810/2009). Note: Mexicans are generally visa-exempt for short Schengen stays, so this binds only visa cases; ETIAS holders are not obliged.

Mexico.cfar_note: No Mexican CFAR figures found. null.

rules.HMO: Must usually choose a PCP and get a referral to see a specialist; out-of-network not covered (except emergencies).
rules.POS: Referral required to see a specialist; out-of-network covered at higher cost.
rules.PPO: No referral needed; in or out of network.

UK.rules: NHS: GP referral needed to see a consultant (specialist); statutory standard 92% of patients start treatment within 18 weeks of referral (RTT). Private: GP referral usually requested by insurers/consultants.

interim_target.text: 65% within 18 weeks by March 2026; 92% by March 2029

england_performance_july_2026.basis: page (list size, %, median via Cover Magazine); search-summary (pathway breakdown, 52/65-week counts, from NHS England press notice which could not be text-extracted)
england_performance_july_2026.note: England only; Scotland/Wales/NI run separate targets not retrieved.

price_private_consultant_initial.note: PHIN: 'around £170 to £250', more for top experts and London; follow-ups often charged the same.

Ireland.rules: Public: GP referral to hospital consultant outpatient clinic; Sláintecare (2017) recommended max 10 weeks for a new outpatient appointment and 12 weeks for inpatient/day case or GI scope. Private: pay consultant directly; private health insurance refunds part (e.g. Vhi EUR 60 per consultation on a cited plan).

ntpf_august_2026_outpatients.note: From a third-party analysis of NTPF open data; gov.ie July 2026 release returned 403.

median_wait_weeks.note: No median outpatient wait figure retrieved.

Canada.rules: Family physician (GP) referral required for a specialist to bill provincial plan at full specialist rate; specialist visit covered by OHIP/MSP, no fee to patient.
Canada.rules_basis: null - general knowledge, no source retrieved for the billing rule; treat as unverified

price_specialist_visit.note: Insured service under provincial plan when referred. Fee-schedule amounts paid to physician not retrieved.

Mexico.rules: IMSS: family doctor (UMF, first level) refers to second-level hospital specialist. Private: no referral needed.

gaps: No fixed published quote for an age-30, one-week trip with a stated trip cost from any named US insurer (all quote dynamically). Squaremouth age-band average exists but its age mapping is ambiguous.
OHIP conflict: ontario.ca (read 2026-10-01) lists 50/400/200 CAD/day limits; news sources say the program ended 1 Jan 2020 except dialysis. Must be resolved against the official page before use.
No state-specific (NY/CA/CT) travel insurance pricing or CFAR availability list; no FAIR Health local figure for a new-patient specialist visit.
Medicare 99204 figure is derived (RVU x conversion factor) from a secondary source; CMS file not opened; no NY/CA/CT locality amounts.
UK sample premiums are search summaries; NHS England press notice PDF could not be text-extracted (figures corroborated by Cover Magazine).
Ireland: no median outpatient wait; gov.ie and Citizens Information returned 403; EHIC validity period unconfirmed.
Canada: BC GP-to-specialist weeks not retrieved; Canadian sample premiums low confidence (age/destination unstated).
